prompt_text:
Storybook ink and gouache with dark contours, slightly realistic, fully painted to the edges, 16:9. Eye-level wide view inside the ground-floor hall of the science faculty: pale tan stone walls, cream stone floor, a glass roof with the faculty telescope's iron gantry visible through it, cool morning daylight, true colors.

Two attached images with different jobs. Image 1 is a planning diagram only: copy each group's position and small size, keep everything named inside its dashed frame; never paint its boxes, lines, words or blank white. Image 2 shows this building from outside: match its tan stone, glass roof, telescope and glass entrance doors, not its aerial viewpoint.

One moment: a geologist is back from fieldwork. His wooden hand-cart stands mid-left, carrying a torn burlap sack of dark earth, soil spilling from the rip, one seedling poking out of the tear. In front of the cart on the floor sits one solid dressed building stone with flat sawn faces and no hole, and a knee-high wooden pier model, a plank deck on four posts, leans against it. Farther back on the left, on a low table, a small cutaway mine model: one tunnel, one lantern, one ore cart on rails.

In the middle foreground, a sparkling mineral cluster on a low round table under a desk lamp throws a small rainbow.

On the right, the geologist, an adult man, sits on a bench and stands his rubber boot in a tray of soil; one worm lifts its head. Behind him, a tall purple crystal on a wooden stand, a teacup-sized mouse at its base.

Back center: open glass doors onto a gravel campus path and autumn trees, threshold clear. Open floor between groups. No other people, no letters.
